text:
alex: heads up — saw a latency regression in canary when kernel-selection switched to the new sampler-based heuristic. 50% tail spike on small batch sizes, looks like H2D wait time balloons. attaching nsys snippet in thread

maria: can you paste the nsys summary? want to see cudaMemcpy H2D breakdown (pageable vs pinned)

alex: paste below — this is an aggregate from a 30s nsys run on the repro (A100, nvlink enabled):
```
nsys stats:
- total H2D memcpy time: 3120ms
- cudaMemcpyAsync H2D (pageable): 1780ms
- cudaMemcpyAsync H2D (pinned): 220ms
- nvlink peer-to-peer copies: 540ms
- kernel execution time: 800ms
- avg small request latency: 12ms -> tail 98th = 85ms
```

jon: interesting — pageable dominates. are we staging host pages for KV cache prefetch? the new kernel picker increases concurrent prefetch tasks?

alex: yes, sampler heuristic increased prefetch parallelism from 8 -> 24 for small sequences (to reduce kernel churn). suspect too many overlapping H2D streams.

akshay: could be PCIe pinned allocation fallback. when pinned pool exhausted, cuda falls back to pageable and implicit pin causes huge stalls. check p2p mempin logs and ioctl faults.

sam: ran a perfetto trace earlier, saw a pattern: bursts of memcpy start, then a long gap where kernels idle waiting on H2D. looks like saturation + serialization on host side.

maria: can you try repro with explicit pinned buffer reuse? quick patch: force host allocation via cudaHostAlloc and reuse per-worker buffer (avoid cudaHostRegister). also limit concurrent prefetchers to 12.

alex: trying now. command used:
```
nsys profile --trace=cuda,cudnn --output=run_pinned --sample=none --duration=35 --target-processes=all ./repro_load --batch-size=1 --prefetchers=24
```

perf-bot: CI run 2016501248 finished — metrics: p50 10ms (-1ms), p95 40ms (+22ms), p99 88ms (+50ms). link: https://ci.example/2016501248

alex: with pinned reuse + prefetchers=12 I see big improvement: total H2D down to 980ms, pageable memcpy ~80ms. new tail p99=28ms.

jon: that suggests our allocator + fallback logic is the culprit. two action items: 1) update sampler to cap concurrent prefetchers by default and 2) add telemetry when pinned pool exhaustion occurs.

akshay: also add microbenchmark that toggles host alloc path (register vs hostalloc) and measures host-to-device memcpy latency and variability under load. I can author it.

maria: also add nsys annotation around host threads that do staging so we can correlate ioctl/page-faults -> memcpy start. perfetto is good but nsys annotations make offline analysis easier.

alex: agreed. I'll open a PR with tests and the quick mitigations (cap prefetchers to 12, reuse pinned buffers). leaving logs in the run artifact: https://artifacts.example/2016501234/nsys

sam: quick note — NVLink p2p copies occupying 540ms earlier — after pinned fix p2p increased (faster), so routing likely changed from host staging to direct p2p. makes sense.

jon: final thought — the kernel-selection heuristic should consider memory path saturation (H2D/P2P util) when picking more parallel prefetchers. otherwise it optimizes for compute parallelism only. add a utilization signal.

alex: will prototype a util-based penalty term for the sampler and run another sweep. thanks y'all :thumbsup:

maria: great catch. can someone add a short postmortem blurb to eng-runtime channel after PR merges? helps ops triage future regressions.

perf-bot: perf regression alert cleared for canary after 2016501302 patch merge.

alex: merging now, will follow up with numbers tomorrow.
